title: Sequential prompt chains
description: The basic chain: the output of prompt 1 becomes the input of prompt 2, step by step (outline -> draft -> revise -> polish). Each link is a small, testable prompt with a clear contract, so failures localize to one link instead of one giant inscrutable prompt.
method: Define links as (prompt_template, input_keys, output_key); run in order, threading outputs; validate each link's output schema before the next link runs.
usage: Keep each link single-purpose; log every link's input/output for replay and debugging.

title: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
description: For consequential chains, the workflow pauses at checkpoints and waits for a human to approve, edit, or reject the intermediate output before continuing. The chain becomes a collaboration: the model drafts, the human decides, the model continues.
method: Mark links as gated; on reaching a gate, the orchestrator persists state and notifies the human; resume applies the human's edited output as the link result.
usage: Gate high-stakes links (external sends, irreversible actions); keep low-stakes links automatic.

demo.code:
state = {'draft': 'Send refund of $50'}
print('CHECKPOINT: draft =', state['draft'])
human = 'approved with edit: $55'
print('human:', human, '-> chain resumes')

title: Conditional retry with fallback prompts
description: When a link's output fails validation, the chain doesn't crash — it retries with a fallback prompt (simpler instructions, a different model, or a repair prompt showing the error). Retries are bounded, and persistent failure routes to a human or a safe default.
method: Validate link output; on failure, retry with the repair prompt (original output + error); after k failures, escalate or use the fallback value.
usage: Make validators strict and repair prompts specific; alert on repeated link failures (a prompt bug, not bad luck).

demo.code:
attempts = ['bad json {', '{"ok": true}']
for i, out in enumerate(attempts):
    ok = out.startswith('{') and out.endswith('}')
    print(f'attempt {i+1}: {"valid" if ok else "invalid -> repair prompt"}')

title: Tool-using chain links
description: Chain links can call tools — search, calculators, code execution, databases — so intermediate steps use real data. A research chain might be: search -> read sources -> synthesize -> cite, with each link's tool calls logged and replayable.
method: Links declare allowed tools; the runtime exposes them as functions; tool results append to the link context as observations.
usage: Scope each link's tool allowlist narrowly; validate tool outputs before they enter the next prompt.

demo.code:
tools = {'search': lambda q: f'results for {q!r}'}
obs = tools['search']('swallow airspeed')
print('tool observation:', obs)
print('next link synthesizes from observation')

title: Chain versioning and A/B testing
description: Prompts are code: chains get versioned (v1.2.3), and traffic splits between versions to measure which performs better on real inputs. Winning versions graduate; losers are kept for rollback. Prompt engineering becomes an experiment, not an argument.
method: Version every prompt template; route a fraction of traffic to the challenger; compare on logged metrics (task success, latency, cost); promote or roll back.
usage: Change one link at a time in challengers so wins are attributable; keep rollback one click away.

title: Streaming chain observability
description: Long chains are black boxes unless instrumented: every link streams its inputs, outputs, token counts, latency, and cost to a trace viewer. When a chain misbehaves in production, the trace shows exactly which link went wrong and what it saw.
method: Wrap each link execution in a span (trace id, link name, timing, tokens, cost); stream spans to the observability backend; render as a waterfall.
usage: Always trace in production (sample if volume is huge); alert on link-level latency or cost anomalies.

demo.code:
spans = [('outline', 1200, 1.2), ('draft', 3400, 4.1), ('polish', 800, 0.6)]
for name, ms, cost in spans:
    print(f'  {name:8} {ms}ms  ${cost:.2f}')
print('trace complete: 3 links, 5.4s, $5.90')

title: Self-critique revision loops
description: The chain generates a draft, then a critic prompt scores it against a rubric and lists flaws, then a reviser fixes them — looping until the critic is satisfied or iterations run out. Draft-critique-revise turns one-shot generation into hill-climbing toward quality.
method: Generate -> critique (rubric scores + flaw list) -> revise addressing flaws; repeat; stop on score threshold or max iterations; keep the best-scoring version.
usage: Write the critic rubric carefully — the loop optimizes exactly what the critic measures.

demo.code:
draft, score = 'v1 draft', 6.0
for i in range(2):
    score += 1.5
    print(f'iteration {i+1}: critic score {score:.1f} -> revise')
print('final: best version kept (score 9.0)')

title: Map-reduce over document sets
description: For long inputs, the chain maps over chunks (summarize each section independently, in parallel) then reduces (combine section summaries into one). Map-reduce chains process arbitrarily long documents with bounded context per call.
method: Split input into chunks; map link runs per chunk in parallel; reduce link merges partial results, possibly hierarchically for very long inputs.
usage: Size chunks to leave headroom for the prompt; reduce hierarchically if partial results overflow context.

demo.code:
chunks = ['sec1 text', 'sec2 text', 'sec3 text']
partials = [f'summary({c})' for c in chunks]
print('mapped:', partials)
print('reduced: combined summary of 3 sections')
